review_text: If you love smelling amazing, then this 2 piece Burberry set review is for you!  First we have Burberry Her, which is such a captivating and feminine scent. These fragrances are not just beautiful on their own, but they also complement each other beautifully when layered. Together they make a unique fragrance that is beautiful and unique! In the time I’ve been using these fragrances, I’ve noticed that I get more compliments when I wear them together. And the best part? A few drops in the morning have lasted me from 7 am to 8 pm during a busy work day. I’ve found that with other fragrances, I often need to reapply midday or even several times throughout the day. But these two have a power and longevity that’s truly impressive. So, whether you’re looking for a fresh, light scent for Spring, or a rich, spicy fragrance for Fall, or even if you’re just looking to expand your fragrance collection, Burberry Her and Goddess are a collection you won’t want to miss.

review_text: My honest review: I did BLIND BUY THIS. I saw this online and all over my tik tok about how it’s a great scent so I took the plunge. I bought the mini just to see. I was nervous but had a feeling I was gonna love this without ever smelling it just knowing the notes in this. A lot of reviews are saying it is super sweet and yes it is but it’s not overpowering at all at least for me. It’s not artificial smelling at all. If you DO NOT like sweet scents this may not be for you. buttt if you do like sweet scents I’m sure you’ll love it. The best way I can describe the smell is like a strawberry milkshake that’s toasted which I know doesn’t exist, but it has a light toasted smell to it. I definitely can smell the fluffy marshmallow, as well as small hints of coconut and vanilla.   This will be my new go to perfume now and when I run out I’m definitely buying the bigger size. I find it pairs well with my mod vanilla and I can’t wait to try it with the Sol de Janeiro 59 :)

review_text: Worth the hype! Scrumptious. I wasn’t sure if I’d like this based on some reviews, but I am obsessed. It starts out sweet strawberry milk shake, within an hour it dries down to the yummiest gourmand marshmallow vanilla with a hint of strawberry. To those who say it doesn’t last, I sprayed it on a jacket 4 days ago and can still smell it. Nice sillage - I get whiffs of it often when wearing and as I pass the jacket I’ll get whiffs of it. I keep reaching for it over my other perfumes, prob bc I keep smelling it on my clothes and it smells amazing. I’ve heard there’s a body spray dupe from bath & bodyworks (haven’t tried it so idk if that’s accurate), but I love that this brand is clean and feel safer spraying clean, high quality ingredients on my body. I’d also say the scent probably lasts a lot longer than a body spray. I love it alone, and also love it layered with another new fav - Clean’s Whipped Cherry (think fans of this will like that perfume too). It’s versatile and I think could be layered with a lot of my other favs to create a custom scent. I also like this brand in particular due to their charitable efforts. All in all, it’s my new fav next to whipped cherry and worth every bit of the hype. And it does smell like Cloud Pink, but I think Cloud Pink is a bit more tropical and doesn’t have anywhere near the lasting power (bought both to compare - returned cloud pink despite it being cheaper).

review_text: This perfume was by far, hands down, without question the best present I got for Christmas this year! I can’t believe I’m saying this, but there is a small, yet very real chance that Boujee Marshmallow may knock the KAYALI GOAT, Pistachio Gelato, out of the #1 spot for my all-time favorite scent. In terms of the scent itself, 5 stars, without a doubt. But, if I was able to award 1/2 stars, I’d be rating it at a 4.5 overall, just for the simple reason that for being an “eau de perfume INTENSE”, it doesn’t last quite as long as I was hoping. It is notably longer lasting than my Pistachio Gelato, which I need to reapply 3-4 times in a day (every 4 hours or so) if I want noticeable scent for 12 hours, and though this one is still “there” after 6 hours, it’s only a very very faint wisp of scent, rather than the bold, freshly-sprayed intensity that I’d like it to be. Someone would have to have their nose directly touching my neck to be able to smell it after 6 hours. But…even with this being the case, it still deserves a full 5 stars because giving it 4 stars wouldn’t be giving it the praise it truly does deserve. The scent profile is absolutely incredible, and because of that, I’ll happily spend a bit more to replenish my stock more often, as I’ll reapply 1-2 times per day in order to keep the scent level at the intensity where I, personally, want it to be. And I’m fine with that. Overall, I absolutely recommend, and I absolutely, WITHOUT QUESTION, will purchase this product again and again and again.

review_text: Every note in this fragrance told me that it would be the opposite of what I usually gravitate towards (which is woody florals and chypres), but I decided to try it anyways. Oh boy, was I in for a surprise. This starts out smelling very youthful in the opening with a burst of strawberry, and I thought it would stay that way. I was wrong. The dry-down is a beautifully balanced powdery marshmallow with a hint of musk and tartness from lingering strawberry. Even my husband who doesn’t like gourmand scents loved this. In his words, it was “perfectly balanced“ and I have to agree! Most Kayali fragrances are pretty standard “good“ but I think the YUM series (Boujie Marshmell and Pistachio Gelato) are standouts. My only critique is that I wished this lasted longer on the skin and that the strawberry popped a little more (though it does last longer than some other Kayali fragrances).

review_text: I generally am not a big fan of Kayali fragrances as they are not unique enough or lean synthetic to my nose. So needless to say I didn’t expect much when I ordered it. But the girly girl in me wanted that pink bottle. I was pleasantly surprised and this scent is actually really nice. It opens with an apple note that smells like a sweet apple, but that note dissipates quickly. After a few minutes the scent becomes more linear and smells like strawberry flavored ice cream, through and through. Nothing else stands up as a note in this composition. It’s creamy, fluffy, girly, youthful. No smell of realistic strawberries, more of the vanillic berry desert, strawberry short cake. Very soft, delicate scent, there is a powdery touch to it that makes me think of strawberry flavored nesquik powder. I think this is very pretty and I don’t have anything in my collection that smells similar. I like that it’s soft and wearable and not too complicated. I also like pairing it with my favorite BDK Bouquet de Hongrie, it makes for a very nice combination if I want more complexity. The longevity is ok, it wears close to skin and doesn’t project much, 4-5 hours on skin, slightly more if you overspray. I’m glad it doesn’t smell synthetic. Just overall nice, well rounded scent. If you like gourmand scents and don’t expect something overly complicated, this is worth trying!

review_text: Some of Kayali’s fragrances have been a miss for me, but I ordered this in a travel size because I liked Vanilla 28 and have been searching for a new gourmand fragrance for the holidays. Very glad I took the chance. At first spray I wasn’t sure I would like it -- a strong, cloying blast of strawberry candy followed by an odd note that reminded me of plaster dust, which thankfully faded within a few minutes. After 10-15 minutes, this dries down on my skin to a wonderful marshmallow cream with a little bit of melted strawberry milkshake and some indefinable soft, almost chai-like spiciness lurking in the background. Unlike others, I’m not getting any coconut. The result is sweet and girly but not in your face or saccharine. I like this a lot more than Vanilla 28, which had an artificial note for me in the dry down. Two sprays has moderate projection for the first couple of hours and lasts another 6-8 hours as an increasingly subtle skin scent.

review_text: I generally am not a big fan of Kayali fragrances as they are not unique enough or lean synthetic to my nose. So needless to say I didn’t expect much when I ordered it. But the girly girl in me wanted that pink bottle. I was pleasantly surprised and this scent is actually really nice. It opens with an apple note that smells like a sweet apple, but that note dissipates quickly. After a few minutes the scent becomes more linear and smells like strawberry flavored ice cream, through and through. Nothing else stands up as a note in this composition. It’s creamy, fluffy, girly. No smell of realistic strawberries, more of the vanillic berry desert, strawberry short cake. Very soft, delicate scent, there is a powdery touch to it that makes me think of strawberry flavored nesquik powder. I think this is very pretty and I don’t have anything in my collection that smells similar. I like that it’s soft and wearable and not too complicated. I also like pairing it with my favorite BDK Bouquet de Hongrie, it makes for a very nice combination if I want more complexity. The longevity is ok, it wears close to skin and doesn’t project much, 4-5 hours on skin, slightly more if you overspray. I’m glad it doesn’t smell synthetic. Just overall nice, well rounded scent. If you like gourmand scents and don’t expect something overly complicated, this is worth trying!

review_text: Received this today and am absolutely in love. Within the first spray, you smell a fruity, creamy, strawberry candy. Think strawberries and whipped cream. As it starts to dry down, the marshmallow really starts to shine through, along with a creamy vanilla, and a hint of a coconut note. To me, once fully dried down, smells like a creamy vanilla marshmallow dessert with coconut flakes. Im obsessed. As far as projection and longevity goes, I am VERY impressed. Kayali is notorious for poor longevity/ projection, but this fragrance really shines! I think they upped their game with this one! It’s sweet, girly, and makes you crave dessert. review_text: I love this one! It smells exactly like the notes that are listed which is always something I appreciate (a good fragrance description). It opens with a gentle strawberry accord paired with a subtle light floral accord (notes say freesia - that sounds right)… You can smell that it’s underpinned by a creamy vanilla accord even in the opening so you do get like a delicate strawberry milkshake vibe in the opening and then it fades to a creamy vanilla with slight musk but thankfully it’s not that insanely loud dry woods/musk profile that is kind of popular nowadays that blasts headache inducing levels of Cashmeran and ambroxan in many fragrances… This is a light musk that plays a supporting role for the creamy vanilla (I think to confer a sense of airiness to turn creamy vanilla into something like a marshmallow) rather than a musk that obliterates all the other notes. It’s well done, delicate, sweet but very wearable and not TOO sweet. Performance and sillage  is definitely on the softer side but that is almost unavoidable in this type of pared down fragrance that is mostly creamy vanilla without any powerhouse ingredient to boost it so I’m not mad at it - I like that they have made this pretty straight gourmand without any heavier notes!

review_text: Yum Boujee Marshmallow by Kayali is like a sugary daydream in a bottle. The first spritz hits you with a pop of sweet, juicy strawberries and a little zing from lemon and apple—it’s fresh and fun, like biting into a perfectly ripe fruit salad. But then, the marshmallow kicks in, and it’s all over. It’s soft, fluffy, and just boujee enough to make you feel like you’re wrapped in a pink, sugary cloud. The coconut and whipped vanilla in the middle make it even more addictive, like the scent equivalent of a dessert you can’t stop eating.As it dries down, it gets warm and cozy with raspberry sugar and musk, but it still keeps that playful, marshmallowy vibe. It’s sweet, but not in a way that’ll give you a headache—it’s more “yum” than “ugh.” I love that it’s vegan and cruelty-free because who doesn’t want to smell like a snack without feeling guilty?The bottle is just as extra as the scent, with Kayali’s signature diamond shape and a cap that looks like it belongs on a vanity. It’s definitely a statement piece. If you’re into sweet, gourmand fragrances but don’t want to smell like straight-up candy, this one balances the fluffiness with a little sophistication.

review_text: This is the one! I love sweet fragrances and was hopeful when I tried Kayali’s Vanilla Candy Rock Sugar fragrance that I would love it. It is a more mature version of something we would wear when we were younger…a boujier version if you will! I haven’t tried layering it with the Vanilla Candy Rock Sugar but I have a feeling that could be a great combo!The top notes include marshmallow, strawberry, coconut, freesia, vanilla, and pink musk. It is described as a “warm and sweet” scent and I find this to be an accurate description. If you love a sweet fragrance that still smells like something an adult would wear, I highly recommend this one.

review_text: I’m not normally huge on gourmand scents, but this one smells amazing. The top notes include pink lady apple, Italian lemon, freesia, and nectarine blossom.  On my skin, I primarily got notes of the pink lady apple and freesia. The middle note that stood out the most to me was the pink marshmallow, with a little whiff of strawberry and coconut flakes. I didn’t get too much orange blossom water. This absolutely smelled like pink cotton candy on my skin. On dry down, I got hints of the whipped vanilla, and just a bit of the raspberry sugar, and pink musk. It dried down beautifully and I enjoyed the sweetness of the fragrance. I tend to stay away from gourmand fragrances because they can smell too artificial, but that wasn’t the case with Kayali Yum Boujee Marshmallow. It absolutely smelled like a confectioner’s dream and was sweet and long lasting. It lasted the entire day on my skin.

After a few minutes the marshmallow and strawberry notes really start to shine and the scent levels out. I just love how bougie I feel in this fragrance, as the name implies. As the hours go by and the fragrance wears on, all of the subtleties rise to the top and I get that soft coconut, creamy vanilla and just the slightest musk. review_text: I couldn’t wait to get my hands on Kayali’s latest fragrance release, and let me tell you—it was worth the wait. From the very first spritz, you’re hit with this heavenly mix of fluffy marshmallow sweetness and juicy strawberries, rounded out with creamy vanilla. As someone who loves sweet notes, this fragrance truly spoke to my senses!The initial burst of Pink Lady Apple and Italian Lemon is refreshing but fleeting, giving way to the star of the show: that dreamy pink marshmallow and strawberry blend in the heart of the scent. There’s something so comforting and luxurious about the way the marshmallow intertwines with coconut flakes and strawberry—it’s like an indulgent dessert you’d order at a high-end patisserie, but wearable. And the dry-down? Pure magic! The whipped vanilla and raspberry sugar settle into the skin with a delicate pink musk and a hint of ambrox, creating a warm, inviting finish that lingers beautifully.If you’re a fan of warm, sweet scents that are playful yet sophisticated, Yum Boujee Marshmallow is a must-try. I absolutely love how the sweetness isn’t overwhelming; instead, it layers in such a way that feels both inviting and subtly boujee. This fragrance wraps me in a cloud of sweetness all day long, and I can’t get enough!

review_text: This is a must buy product! I just received my second bottle and I know this is a product I will re-purchase again and again. The first time I used this product I did experience the pilling that other reviews have mentioned. I’ve learned some things along the way that prevent it from happening altogether...- First step: I mist my face with distilled water and then apply The Ordinary Hyaluronic Acid. Then I wait one full minute before moving onto the next step to allow it to fully dry. - I mist my face with distilled water again, then immediately apply 2-3 drops of Niacinamide all over my face and neck. I notice that a damp face allows the product to work into the skin more evenly. - Then... and this is the most IMPORTANT part... WAIT 5 min before moving onto the next step in your skincare routine. Whether that’s a serum, moisturizer or SPF... make sure to incorporate that wait period to allow the Niacinamide to A.) work alone and B.) completely dry. That’s it! No pilling, no problem! Bonus: If you’re feeling EXTRA — I keep my Niacinamide in my skincare fridge and while this step is not necessary at all I swear it helps the consistency of the product and the application as well.

review_text: The Ordinary is an amazing brand if you know how to use the products and properly research them. Their products are meant to be supplemental and used in conjunction with other products to target specific problems, and in that way they are super effective. This Niacinamide   Zinc serum is truly exceptional. Niacinamide is wonderful for restoring skin’s barrier, locking in moisture to help control oil, and therefore, really helps with the fading of dark marks/pigmentation and just improving skins overall texture and evenness. It will also help brighten and plump dull skin too. The zinc really helps with inflammation, calms the skin and reduces any redness from acne or other skin issues, and helps to control oil naturally. So if you have bacterial acne or really oily skin that is hard to manage, adding this to your routine will really help without causing additional irritation or peeling like other acne targeted treatments. I recommend starting this once every other night instead of jumping into using it twice a day right away because some people have said to have negative reactions, which I think is partly caused by either allergic or irritating reactions or misuse/too much use of the product. If you use too much, it can ball up and be difficult and gross underneath makeup. I started off using it that way and quickly learned it’s not effective. If you use ONE or TWO drops in moisturizer, I’ve found that’s the best way to go and your skin will really look much more plump, matte, and healthy after just a week or so of use.I have moderate acne and have suffered with cystic acne, hormonal acne, and whiteheads for the past several years since I hit 25 years old so I have tried everything and learned so much about the ingredients and scientific approach to skincare, that I can knowledgeably say that this is one of the best products to help repair sensitive or acne ravaged skin while preventing new spots due to oil control without irritating or making skin or acne worse.

review_text: I’ve been debating writing this review for a bit because my opinion of this product and experience with how it worked on my skin seems to differ from a lot of others’ experiences with it. This is a product that isn’t meant to heal acne or stop break outs, and I think its marketed incorrectly as a treatment. Another problem I have with this product is that niacinamide is an ingredient that reacts poorly with a lot of the ingredients that can help heal and treat acne/breakouts/blemishes. review_text: I first tried this toner during last year’s Sephora sale when my mom gave me her birthday mini. I have used it since and I enjoyed it so much up until about a few months ago. I am 13 and my skin isn’t acne-prone but my skin barrier isn’t the thickest due to my eczema (and obviously my age). I loved that it smoothed and cleared my skin of impurities. But as the winter started began noticing that my skin became incredibly dry. At one point, it looked like I had aged about 10 years. I believe this was because my skin barrier was thinner than usual due to the changing seasons, and became even weaker because of this product. I still use this product to this day, and I reccomend it, however I advise you use it only once or twice a week as a gentle chemical exfoliant - not a toner. Also, avoid from applying near your undereyes, I noticed that my undereyes began creasing a lot more. At first I thought I wasn’t using the right foundation/concealer/powder, but then I stopped using this product as often and saw that my undereyes appeared much firmer. Overall, please be careful with this product and only use it as an exfoliant, not a toner. Also, make sure you pair it with hydrating products such as serums and moisturizers containing hyaluronic acid.

While I’ve not noticed an improvement in my enlarged clogged pores, longterm, it provides a slight immediate refined and smooth appearance, and I will continue to use and purchase just because it’s such a treat for my skin..Now that my go-to nourishing toner has been discontinued, it’ll serve as replacement. review_text: This is my first time purchasing Glow Recipe and I wasn’t impressed.  I really just found this to be an awkward formulation because, while the premise of combining exfoliating PHA+BHA with hydrating cactus water, etc., seems to make sense (so that the astringent acids are supposedly balanced out by the watermelon and hyaluronic acid), in actuality what this gives you is a strong dose of exfoliation/astringency that does strip your skin of some of its usual hydration and oils which the watermelon, cucumber, and hyaluronic acid can’t make up for because those molecules aren’t small enough to deeply penetrate your skin but will block the passage of subsequent skincare products.  So, using this product as your first-step toner in the long run, you’re putting something quite aggressive on your skin and then not able to sufficiently nourish your skin afterward which makes for stressed, malnourished, and prone to wrinkling skin.  The first couple weeks using this product yields good results because, yes, the PHA+BHA are doing their work, but then I started noticing progressive dryness and peeling.  It just seems like this product wasn’t thought through very well.I also disliked the candy-like scent of the product and its packaging which is simply cheap and unattractive.  For a product of this price and size, a bumpy glass bottle and plastic cap just seem inadequate.  And, given its overall value due to the formulation, I wouldn’t buy this again and do not recommend.

So what IS this? PHA, or Poly Hydroxy Acids are a group of acids that work their magic slowly, which is great for sensitive skin that is prone to irritation and redness (which befuddles me as to why it does NOT help me). And BHA stands for beta hydroxy acid. BHAs are water-soluble acids made from sugary fruits. They help peel away the surface of your skin so that new, more evenly pigmented skin cells may generate and take their place.You would *THINK* that this toner would help my irritated skin, but alas, it doesn’t. My irritated areas peel, and true to the BHA, the peeling gets WORSE. With that said, I am enjoying the benefits from the scent and the pore cleaning/tightening on my nose and between said nose and cheeks.

review_text: Will be the moisturizer I will use FOREVER! In recent years I have found myself thoroughly frustrated with the skincare industry & the US’s regulation of it. Companies are allowed to place just about anything in our products. As a medical esthetician, who took the time to really study ingredients, where they are derived, what they do & how, I have found myself reading thousands (not kidding) of product ing. lists thinking, “This is not touching my skin!I am severly acne-prone & sensitive (hormones, ugh) I can’t use even the most noncomedogenic oils on my skin, they will all eventually clog my pores. I need an oil-free moisturer that does not contain ingredients that will irritated my sensituve skin or break me out. It is almost an impossible task! Even products claiming to be “clean“ & free of nasties like parabens, pthlates, petroleum based ingredients, etc etc, usually still contain fractionated oils (like capric/caprylic triglyceride, which is altered palm or coconut oil), silicones (which while not comedogenic in & of themselves, do seal things that are against the skin, like your own dead skin cells & sebum), alcohols (drying, except for a few, like cetyl, stearyl, cetearyl, which are fatty alcohols, but they are comedogenic). Stumbling across this product was great. I find it moisturizes my combo skin well, no irritation, helps barrier function, has anti-inflammatories for soothing breakout & light acids for exfoliating. If some of those ingredients look scary, they aren’t, promise. My only issue is with “fragrance“ at the bottom. It contains lots of plant & fruit extracts (just be careful if you have allergies, read all of them), plus: Gluconolactone is a PHA, polyhydroxy acid, that exfoliates gentler than AHAs;Sodium Polyglutamate is similar to HA in that it draws moisture, but also help your acid mantle & is anti-inflammatory; &Betaine Salicylate is a gentle acid, milder than salicylic acid, another beta-hydroxy acid.
